target_customer: Third party app developers and small businesses wanting to accept in person card payments through their own software
problem: Apps could not easily accept card present payments; Square controlled the whole experience, and developers wanted an open API with a card reader.
business_model: Usage based payments API with transaction fees of 2.5 percent plus 10 cents card present and 2.9 percent plus 30 cents card not present, per TechCrunch in July 2013

founders.name: Charlie Pinto
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as WePay employee number 12 and later at Google Domains and Bling Capital; the Google Domains and Bling roles came after SlidePay. Degree not listed.

founders.name: Christopher Morton
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page with no background.

founders.name: Joel Christner
founders.background_notes: YC page lists interests in distributed systems and data management; no employers or education.

competitors.name: Square
competitors.what: Card reader and point of sale with a closed, controlled customer experience
competitors.traction_then: Market leader in mobile card readers

technical_complexity.rationale: Offering a payments API with its own merchant account, underwriting and identity verification (per TechCrunch) required payments and compliance work beyond a typical small team app.

defensibility.rationale: Owning the merchant account and underwriting had some friction, but competitors such as Square and Stripe could and did offer similar developer tooling.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it; the company was acquired in 2014 by a non payments firm, Rocket Lawyer, per aggregators.

market_need_then: Developer apps such as Joist wanted to add card present payments inside their own flow; TechCrunch cited that example in 2013 but gave no volumes.

branding.domain_note: The listed website is an Angel.co page that redirects to Wellfound, which suggests no standalone site remained; not fetched further.

identity.voice_and_tone: Developer focused, positioned as the Android of payments against Square's Apple-like approach

branding.brand_signature: Android of payments positioning in TechCrunch headline

rebrands.why: Renamed with the pivot from a point of sale system to a developer payments API; no source states the naming reason.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community evidence beyond one launch article; the name is a descriptive compound.

pivots.from: Cube, a point of sale system for small businesses
pivots.to: SlidePay, a payments API for third party developers
pivots.why: CEO said the goal was to let people provide their own applications, as an open alternative to Square.

outcome_analysis: Cube started as a point of sale system, pivoted by mid 2013 to SlidePay, a developer payments API aimed at being the open alternative to Square. It raised about 1.3 million dollars per aggregators and was acquired in 2014 by Rocket Lawyer for an undisclosed amount. Whether it was a real product outcome or a soft landing is not public; the acquihire label is an inference from the small team and unusual buyer.
notes: Exit date conflicts: YC says October 2014, PitchBook via Dealroom says 2014-01-01, CB Insights says 2014-12. Acquirer Rocket Lawyer comes from aggregators only and CB Insights words it as Rocket Lawyer investing in an acquired round, so it is unverified. Funding total conflicts: 1.3M (CB Insights, Seedtable) vs 800K (Dealroom). The angel.co website was not opened past its redirect. As_of is 2013-07 because the earliest source about SlidePay as an API is that article; Cube competition at the batch is not documented. failure_factors acquihire_soft_landing is a low confidence judgment.
